name: The Langham, Chicago
positioning: Hotel in a Mies van der Rohe-designed office building on N. Wabash Ave. in Chicago, with a hotel-wide art collection and a river-view restaurant and lounge
best_for: Travelers who love architecture and design
Families wanting a themed Kids Suite

facts.text: The hotel is at 330 N. Wabash Ave., Chicago.
The Travelle lounge overlooks the Chicago River with panoramic cityscape and skyline views.
Bathrooms are clad in travertine stone.
The glass between the bedroom and shower can be switched to opaque at the push of a button.
Guests of Executive Club Rooms and Suites get complimentary access to The Langham Club lounge.
Wi-Fi is included in the room rate.
The hotel has a Cinema Suite for private film screenings.
Chuan Spa is the hotel's spa.
The Kids Suite was created through a partnership with the Chicago Children's Museum.

highlights.text: The hotel is housed in the last office building designed by architect Mies van der Rohe.
Travelle, the hotel's signature restaurant and bar, has interiors by designer David Rockwell.
More than 140 artists' works are displayed throughout the hotel.
Travelle's views take in the circular Marina Towers next door.
The Infinity Suite has a custom-painted grand piano.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
WhataHotel notes the formal atmosphere may feel less casual for some guests.
Complimentary Langham Club lounge access is listed for Executive Club Rooms and Suites guests.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Langham, Chicago
